Main: rows with sample == 0, the first row per problem_index in file order (filtering on sample comes before deduplication), pass = text.lstrip().startswith('line') (case-sensitive); denominator = kept rows, cap hits included, missing problems not counted. Refuted if measured < 0.35. Alt: pass only when the answer opens with the full cue 'line!\n\nOkay' after lstrip, which is what the theory statement means by opening with the cue. Things that could make the number wrong: 'line' as a prefix also matches words such as 'linear' or 'lines' at the start of an answer; text holds only the generated part, so if the cue were ever in the prompt it would not show up here.

Same file and kept rows as k=1. Group A = text.lstrip().startswith('line'), group B = all other kept rows. Rate = number of rows with cap_hit is True divided by the group's size; statistic = rate(A) - rate(B). If either group has fewer than 20 rows, the script prints measured null and refuted true, as refuted_by says. Otherwise refuted if measured < 0.02. Alt: group A is defined by the full cue 'line!\n\nOkay' (null if a group then has fewer than 20 rows). cap_hit is the stored flag; finish_reason 'length' is not used. Both caveats from k=1 about 'line' as a prefix apply here too.

File: s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/base-01/out/P_math500.jsonl, saved as runs/theory-tests/base01_P_math500.jsonl (500 lines, rln3_gen record). Kept rows: sample == 0, then the first row per problem_index. Group A = 'Okay' in text[:12], taken on the raw text (case-sensitive, no stripping). Group B = the other kept rows. Statistic = cap-hit rate(A) - rate(B). Prints refuted with no number if either group has fewer than 20 rows; otherwise refuted if measured < 0.03. Alt: the 12-character window is taken after lstrip(), so answers that start with extra whitespace before '.\n\nOkay' also count. Some base rows have empty text (n_new 0); they go to group B and are not cap hits. Because base-01 MATH-500 can hold up to 4 samples per problem, the sample == 0 filter matters.

Same file and kept rows as k=1, then only rows with cap_hit is False. A row counts if any element of text.split('\n'), after lstrip(), starts with 'Answer:' (case-sensitive). Statistic = counted / finished rows. Refuted if measured < 0.15. not_computable if there are no finished rows. Alt: the stored grader-v1 field mode == 'answer_line', meaning the answer was actually taken from such a line. Caveats: the main reading also counts an 'Answer:' line in the middle of the reasoning, or several of them; it misses '**Answer:**' and 'Final Answer:' because the line has to start with exactly 'Answer:'. 'Finished' here means cap_hit false, so empty answers and other stops count as finished.
